question: Which sentence uses "row" to mean a fight or noisy argument?

options.text: We had a terrible row last night.
He rowed the boat across the lake.
They sat in the front row.
There were ten chairs in each row.

solution:
**The correct answer is: Option 1) We had a terrible row last night.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Row** in this context refers to a fight or noisy argument. (झगड़ा, शोरगुल भरी बहस)

 
 
• **Example:** We had a terrible row last night.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **We had a terrible row last night.**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their meanings:

 
• **He rowed the boat across the lake.** (खेवना): In this sentence, "rowed" refers to the action of propelling a boat with oars.
 
• **They sat in the front row.** (पंक्ति): Here, "row" refers to a line or sequence of seats.
 
• **There were ten chairs in each row.** (पंक्ति): In this context, "row" also means a line or sequence of items, specifically chairs.
